findings: Structurally normal heart. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.

general.summary: No directly applicable, high-quality evidence was retrieved for this query. Recommend correlating with current society guidelines.

mri.impression: No acute intracranial abnormality. No mass, haemorrhage, midline shift, or restricted diffusion. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age.

output.interpretation: Lumbar puncture, hospital day 6. Opening pressure 142 mmH2O (normal). Nucleated cells 2/mm3. Protein 78 mg/dL (elevated). Glucose 62 mg/dL (CSF:serum ratio 0.60). Gram stain: no organisms. Elevated protein with a normal cell count (albuminocytological dissociation). Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Bedside respiratory function on hospital day 6: FVC 1.9 L (68% predicted; 23 mL/kg at 81 kg) L. MIP -30 cmH2O L. MEP 46 cmH2O L. Cough effective.

events.event: Sinus rate 58 bpm during sleep, self-limited, no pause

output.impression: 24-hour continuous telemetry. Sinus rhythm with sinus tachycardia while awake (maximum 108 bpm) and a self-limited sinus rate of 58 bpm during sleep. No pauses and no sustained arrhythmia. Blood pressure 136/80 to 176/98 mmHg.
output.rhythm_summary: Sinus rhythm: tachycardia while awake, slower rate during sleep.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Polyradiculoneuropathy pattern (demyelinating or axonal features, absent F-waves, sural sparing where present); may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Nerve conduction studies and needle EMG
action_criteria.rationale: Nerve conduction studies support the diagnosis and separate a peripheral cause of the new weakness from a central one [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Albuminocytological dissociation: raised protein with cells <5/mm3 (5-50/mm3 compatible but prompts an alternative; >50/mm3 suggests another diagnosis); protein may be normal in the first week
action_criteria.label: Lumbar puncture for CSF cell count, protein and glucose
action_criteria.rationale: The day 1 lumbar puncture was done to exclude infection before the neurological picture appeared; CSF protein and cells now support the diagnosis [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Sodium corrected to 132 mEq/L with low serum osmolality (persisting mild hyponatraemia); normal potassium, liver tests, albumin and CK; baseline values before IVIg
action_criteria.label: Baseline blood tests: full blood count, renal function and electrolytes, liver tests, albumin, glucose and CK
action_criteria.rationale: Routine blood tests give the baseline before IVIg and the current sodium, which IVIg can lower; potassium and CK exclude metabolic mimics [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: FVC in L, % predicted and mL/kg, MIP and MEP, with the trend; ICU-level monitoring if FVC <20 mL/kg or <60% predicted, MIP weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP <40 cmH2O, a fall of more than 30%, or bulbar weakness with weak cough
action_criteria.label: Bedside respiratory function (FVC, MIP, MEP), repeated serially while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Weakness began on day 6 and is spreading to the arms in a patient with COPD; serial FVC, MIP and MEP decide ICU-level monitoring [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Continuous telemetry with blood pressure monitoring: sinus tachycardia to 108 bpm while awake, a sinus rate of 58 bpm in sleep and blood pressure 136/80 to 176/98 mmHg in the first 24 hours; autonomic instability (rate and blood pressure lability, bradyarrhythmia) requires continued monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.label: Continuous inpatient cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses
action_criteria.rationale: Autonomic dysfunction is common in GBS and can cause bradyarrhythmias and blood-pressure lability; monitoring continues while weakness progresses [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal sinus rhythm 92 bpm with normal intervals (QTc 452 ms) and no conduction or repolarisation abnormality: a baseline while autonomic involvement can still develop
action_criteria.label: Obtain a 12-lead ECG to screen for autonomic dysrhythmias and baseline QTc
action_criteria.rationale: A baseline 12-lead ECG screens for autonomic dysrhythmia and conduction abnormality and gives the QTc before treatment [EAN_PNS_2023].

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Thiazide already stopped; losartan and hypotension with plasma exchange as a relative caution; IVIg and measured sodium
action_criteria.label: Optional interaction check of losartan, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin and tiotropium before IVIg or plasma exchange
action_criteria.rationale: The only management-changing drug, hydrochlorothiazide, was stopped on admission; the check does not change the IVIg or plasma exchange decision.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General evidence on immunotherapy in GBS; not needed for the diagnosis or the treatment decision
action_criteria.label: Optional literature search on IVIg versus plasma exchange in GBS
action_criteria.rationale: Background evidence only; not a clinical step of the work-up.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not treat with corticosteroids: oral corticosteroids are strongly advised against and IV methylprednisolone is not recommended [EAN_PNS_2023].
Do not give hypertonic saline for a fall in measured sodium during IVIg without checking serum osmolality (pseudohyponatraemia).
Do not start IVIg without checking renal function.
required_recommendations: Move to ICU-level monitoring: MIP is at -30 cmH2O, weakness is spreading to the arms and COPD limits her reserve (FVC 68% predicted, 23 mL/kg, MEP 46 cmH2O). Repeat FVC, MIP and MEP every 2-4 hours and intubate if FVC falls below 20 mL/kg (about 1.6 L at 81 kg), MIP becomes weaker than -30 cmH2O, MEP falls below 40 cmH2O, bulbar weakness with weak cough appears, or respiratory distress, hypoxaemia or hypercapnia develop [Lawn_2001, EAN_PNS_2023].

Start IVIg 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total, about 32 g/day at 81 kg) now, within 2 weeks of onset, because she cannot walk unaided (GBS disability score 3); plasma exchange (200-250 mL/kg over 5 sessions) is an equivalent alternative [EAN_PNS_2023].

Keep hydrochlorothiazide stopped and continue fluid restriction; check sodium with serum osmolality every 12-24 hours during IVIg (SIADH can persist in GBS, and IVIg can lower the measured sodium), limiting any further correction to 8-10 mEq/L in 24 hours.
Continuous cardiac telemetry with blood pressure monitoring while weakness progresses.
Pharmacological DVT prophylaxis (subcutaneous low-molecular-weight heparin) while she cannot walk [Leonhard_2019].

avoided_actions.rationale: Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
A head CT was normal on admission and CT does not show nerve roots; the new deficit is peripheral.

Brain MRI was done on admission. The new deficit is lower motor neuron (flaccid weakness, areflexia, sensory loss) without bulbar, pseudobulbar or long-tract signs, so it does not suggest osmotic demyelination or another central cause.
An EEG on admission showed diffuse slowing without epileptiform activity, and the encephalopathy resolved with sodium correction; a repeat EEG does not address the new peripheral deficit.

accepted: Guillain-Barré syndrome, AIDP, presenting with severe SIADH-related hyponatraemia and delayed motor signs

differential.diagnosis: SIADH or thiazide-associated hyponatraemia as the sole cause
differential.key_features: Explained the admission encephalopathy, which resolved with correction, but cannot explain flaccid ascending weakness with areflexia, CSF albuminocytological dissociation and demyelinating conduction appearing on day 6. Hyponatraemia can be a feature of GBS.

Correction reached 10 mEq/L in 24 hours, but the deficit is lower motor neuron with sensory loss and areflexia, there are no bulbar, pseudobulbar or long-tract signs, and the NCS and CSF show a polyradiculoneuropathy.
The encephalopathy resolved with sodium correction and there have been no seizures; it would not explain areflexic weakness.

differential.diagnosis: Spinal cord or cauda equina compression
differential.key_features: Back pain preceded the leg symptoms, but the arms are weak, there is no sensory level or sphincter dysfunction, and the NCS shows diffuse demyelination.
Cannot be excluded at presentation; progression beyond 8 weeks or 3 or more treatment-related fluctuations would point to it. Reassess at 8 weeks.

key_clinical_evidence: Flaccid ascending weakness with areflexia appearing on day 6, CSF albuminocytological dissociation (protein 78 mg/dL, 2 cells/mm3) and a demyelinating NCS: GBS, presenting with hyponatraemia.
GBS can cause SIADH; profound hyponatraemia may dominate the presentation and delay the neurological diagnosis.
A lower motor neuron deficit with sensory loss and areflexia argues against osmotic demyelination, which causes bulbar, pseudobulbar and long-tract signs.
IVIg can lower the measured sodium (pseudohyponatraemia from the protein load); check serum osmolality before treating a fall in sodium during IVIg.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: The encephalopathy resolved with correction; the later flaccid areflexic weakness with sensory loss, CSF albuminocytological dissociation and demyelinating NCS is GBS, which can itself cause SIADH. The thiazide may have contributed to the hyponatraemia.
red_herrings.data_point: Profound hyponatraemia (Na 110 mEq/L) with encephalopathy on admission
red_herrings.intended_effect: Attributes the whole illness to hyponatraemia, its treatment or osmotic demyelination, and delays recognition of the neuropathy.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Back and radicular pain is common at the onset of GBS; arm weakness, absent sensory level and sphincter symptoms, and the diffuse demyelinating NCS place the lesion in the nerves and roots.
red_herrings.data_point: New lower back pain before the leg symptoms
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests a spinal or cauda equina lesion.

interactions: Hydrochlorothiazide: thiazides cause hyponatraemia with a urine picture resembling SIADH; listed as stopped.

IVIg: the protein load can lower measured sodium without lowering serum osmolality (pseudohyponatraemia); sucrose- or maltose-containing products can cause true dilutional hyponatraemia (monitor sodium with serum osmolality).
Losartan: additive hypotension with the fluid shifts of plasma exchange (relative caution).
Tiotropium: antimuscarinic; can worsen urinary retention.
Atorvastatin: no interaction with IVIg or plasma exchange.
general.proposed: IVIg or plasma exchange with the current medication list
general.summary: Category-level review of losartan, hydrochlorothiazide, atorvastatin and tiotropium against IVIg and plasma exchange.

ecg.interpretation: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 92. Normal intervals (QTc 452 ms). No acute ST-T wave changes.

labs.interpretation: Sodium 132 mEq/L (low). Serum osmolality 274 mOsm/kg (low). Creatinine 0.4 mg/dL (low). Glucose 104 mg/dL (elevated). WBC 11.4 x10^9/L (elevated). Remaining values within reference ranges.

results.finding: Guidelines for adults with GBS who cannot walk unaided advise IVIg 2 g/kg over 5 days within 2 weeks of onset or plasma exchange within 4 weeks, with no preference between them; corticosteroids are not advised.
A second IVIg course in patients with a poor predicted prognosis did not improve outcome and caused more serious adverse events.

general.summary: IVIg or plasma exchange is advised for adults with GBS unable to walk unaided; neither is preferred, and a second IVIg course is not advised [EAN_PNS_2023, Walgaard_2021].

findings.finding: DML 7.8 ms (prolonged); CV 28 m/s (reduced); CMAP 2.0 mV (reduced)
DML 8.2 ms (prolonged); CV 26 m/s (reduced); CMAP 1.6 mV (reduced)
DML 6.8 ms (prolonged); CV 36 m/s (reduced); CMAP 4.6 mV
Absent bilateral peroneal and tibial; prolonged bilateral median
Tibialis anterior, vastus lateralis and first dorsal interosseous bilaterally: reduced recruitment of normal-morphology motor units; no fibrillation potentials or positive sharp waves

specialized_test.impression: This is an ABNORMAL study. 1. Markedly prolonged distal motor latencies and reduced conduction velocities in peroneal, tibial and median motor nerves, with reduced lower limb CMAP amplitudes. 2. Absent F-waves (peroneal, tibial) and prolonged median F-waves; absent H-reflexes. 3. Absent sural sensory nerve action potentials. 4. Reduced recruitment without denervation on needle EMG. Findings meet electrodiagnostic criteria for an acute demyelinating polyradiculoneuropathy. Clinical correlation recommended.

metadata.difficulty_description: GBS presenting as profound hyponatremic encephalopathy (Na 110), with motor and sensory signs emerging on day 6 after sodium correction; osmotic demyelination and a thiazide are the competing explanations.
metadata.difficulty_rationale: 5 required actions, 2 red herrings; a metabolic presentation that hides the neuropathy and a correction history that invites a central explanation.
metadata.revision_reason: Reviewer 2 GBS audit: spine MRI is optional and limited to five cases with a concrete cord, traumatic, postoperative or infiltrative alternative; generic hidden MRI reports removed.

patient.chief_complaint: Bilateral leg weakness and numbness on hospital day 6, after admission with profound hyponatremic encephalopathy.

family_history: Hypertension in family; no neurological disease

patient.history_present_illness: Ms. R. is a 64-year-old woman admitted 6 days ago after her neighbor found her unresponsive at home. The day before, she had mild malaise, decreased appetite and mild stomach discomfort. On arrival she was obtunded (GCS 9) with confused speech. Serum sodium was 110 mEq/L (136 mEq/L three months earlier on the same medications), serum osmolality 235 mOsm/kg, urine osmolality 413 mOsm/kg and urine sodium 76 mEq/L; TSH and morning cortisol were normal and the WBC was 18.1 x10^9/L. CT of the head was normal. Brain MRI on admission showed scattered nonspecific T2 hyperintensities without changes of osmotic demyelination, and an EEG showed diffuse slowing without epileptiform discharges. A lumbar puncture on day 1 showed no infection and empiric antibiotics were stopped. Hydrochlorothiazide was stopped and she was treated with hypertonic saline and fluid restriction; sodium rose from 110 to 120 mEq/L over the first 24 hours. On admission there was no limb weakness and her reflexes were documented as diminished. By day 5 she was oriented and was transferred to the ward. On day 6 she reported new lower back pain followed by numbness and tingling of both legs, then difficulty standing and walking. She has no bladder or bowel symptoms, no difficulty swallowing and no shortness of breath beyond her usual exertional breathlessness from COPD.

neurological_exam.additional: Lower back pain without spinal tenderness. No bladder or bowel dysfunction.
neurological_exam.coordination: Mild limb ataxia, out of proportion to the weakness in the arms.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Intact. No facial weakness, no dysarthria or dysphagia. Eye movements full.
neurological_exam.gait: Cannot walk safely without bilateral support.
neurological_exam.motor: Lower limbs: hip flexion 3/5, knee extension 3+/5, ankle dorsiflexion 3/5 bilaterally. Upper limbs: shoulder abduction 4/5, grip 4/5 bilaterally. Normal strength before admission according to her family.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Patellar 1+ and Achilles absent bilaterally; biceps and brachioradialis 1+ bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Bilateral distal tingling and numbness; reduced light touch in both lower limbs below the knees. No sensory level.
